policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'with certain elders' renders the indefinite τινῶν; the articular τῶν πρεσβυτέρων would give 'the elders'.
ASV 'evils are corrected for this nation' renders διορθωμάτων (corrections/reforms); κατορθωμάτων would be successful achievements, i.e. 'worthy deeds are done'.
ASV plural 'a mover of insurrections' renders στάσεις; the singular στάσιν would give 'insurrection'.
ASV ends the verse at 'on whom also we laid hold:' with nothing answering the TR continuation about judging by our law, Lysias' intervention, or commanding the accusers to come before thee.
τε and δὲ are both carried by ASV's opening 'And'; the English connective does not distinguish them.
ASV 'I cheerfully make my defence' renders the positive εὐθύμως; the comparative εὐθυμότερον would give 'the more cheerfully'.
ASV 'canst take knowledge' fits either the compound ἐπιγνῶναι or the simplex γνῶναι; the English does not mark the prefix.
δώδεκα and δεκαδύο are alternate spellings of the same numeral, both rendered 'twelve'.
ASV 'to worship at Jerusalem' is compatible with either εἰς or ἐν; the preposition after 'went up' is not differentiated in the English.
ASV 'stirring up a crowd' fits both ἐπίστασιν and ἐπισύστασιν, which carry the same sense of raising a mob.
ASV 'Neither can they prove' renders οὐδὲ and οὔτε alike; the negative conjunction is not distinguished in English.
ASV 'Neither can they prove to thee the things' has no object answering RP's added με; the only 'me' in the verse renders κατηγοροῦσίν μου at the end.
ASV 'prove to thee' renders σοι, which RP omits.
νυνὶ and νῦν are both rendered 'now'; the emphatic form is not marked in English.
ASV 'and which are written in the prophets' reads the same whether the dative is governed by τοῖς ἐν or stands alone as τοῖς προφήταις γεγραμμένοις.
ASV 'there shall be a resurrection both of the just and unjust' has nothing answering RP's added νεκρῶν, 'of the dead'.
ASV 'Herein I also exercise myself' renders the adverbial καὶ as 'also'; δὲ would give an adversative connective and no 'also'.
ASV 'exercise myself to have a conscience' renders the infinitive ἔχειν as complement; the participle ἔχων would give 'exercise myself, having a conscience'.
The candidates differ only in the placement of παρεγενόμην; English requires the finite verb first in 'I came to bring alms to my nation', so the ASV does not witness the Greek order.
αἷς and οἷς differ only in the gender of the relative; ASV 'amidst which' renders either.
ASV 'who ought to have been here before thee' renders the past ἔδει; the present δεῖ would give 'who ought to be here'.
ἐμέ and με are emphatic and enclitic forms of the same pronoun, both rendered 'me' after 'against'.
ASV 'what wrong-doing they found when I stood before the council' has nothing answering the added ἐν ἐμοὶ, 'in me'.
The candidates differ only in the order of ἑστὼς and ἐν αὐτοῖς; ASV 'I cried standing among them' renders either order.
ASV 'I am called in question before you this day' renders ἐφ᾽ ὑμῶν, 'before you'; ὑφ᾽ ὑμῶν would give the agent 'by you'.
ASV 'But Felix, having more exact knowledge concerning the Way, deferred them' has no rendering of RP's Ἀκούσας δὲ ταῦτα, 'and when he had heard these things'.
εἴπας and εἰπών are alternate aorist participle forms of the same verb, both rendered 'saying'.
ASV's sentence-initial 'And he gave order' is the ordinary English start of a new sentence and does not show whether RP's connective τε stood in the Greek.
ASV 'that he should be kept in charge' renders the pronoun αὐτόν; RP's τὸν Παῦλον would give the name, which the ASV renders elsewhere in the chapter when it stands.
ASV 'to minister unto him' has nothing answering RP's added ἢ προσέρχεσθαι, 'or to come to him'.
The ASV note 'Greek his own wife.' attests ἰδίᾳ in the underlying text, which RP omits.
ASV 'the faith in Christ Jesus' renders Ἰησοῦν, which the competing reading omits.
ASV 'the judgment to come' renders μέλλοντος alone or μέλλοντος ἔσεσθαι identically; the added infinitive leaves no English trace.
ASV 'money would be given him of Paul: wherefore also he sent for him the oftener' has nothing answering RP's added ὅπως λύσῃ αὐτόν, 'that he might loose him'.
ASV 'desiring to gain favor with the Jews' uses 'favor' as a mass noun, which renders singular χάριτα and plural χάριτας alike.
